claims.text: In single-phase high-entropy superconducting alloys, Tc is primarily governed by average valence electron count.
Average valence electron count modulates electron–phonon coupling strength.
Increasing VEC through isostructural substitution enhances electron–phonon coupling.
Increasing VEC will raise Tc if the solid solution and controlled disorder are maintained.
The target material is a single-phase solid solution containing at least five elements, each at no less than 5 atomic percent.
Selecting a replacement element with a similar atomic radius can preserve the single-phase structure during VEC adjustment.
Identical processing and sintering histories ensure that only electronic-structure differences affect superconductivity.
Local lattice distortions and chemical disorder are inherent to multielement mixing in HEAs.
Local lattice distortions and chemical disorder modulate the electronic density of states.
Local lattice distortions and chemical disorder modulate electron–phonon coupling and superconducting behavior.
Increasing average VEC enhances the electron density near the Fermi level.
A higher density of states near the Fermi level produces stronger electron–phonon interactions.
Stronger electron–phonon interactions favor superconducting pairing.
Tc exhibits correlations or systematic trends with electron count in previously studied HEA superconductors.
Excessive substitution may produce strong lattice distortion or phase instability.
Strong disorder or substitution-induced instability can degrade or suppress superconductivity.
Magnetic impurities and strong electronic correlations can interfere with the proposed VEC-controlled behavior.
A failure of Tc to increase systematically with VEC, in samples that remain phase stable, would falsify the proposed governing relationship.

contradictions.description: The conditions claim that identical processing ensures only electronic-structure differences, whereas the proposed mediator and predicted outcome allow substitution-dependent changes in lattice distortion, disorder, and phase stability. Thus the intervention is not demonstrated to isolate VEC from structural changes.
